definition_of_done: src/hello/byte_counter.py defines count_bytes(data: bytes) -> int, which returns len(data).
hello.byte_counter performs no file, process or console I/O and imports only the standard library.

Running `wordcount PATH` on a readable UTF-8 file prints exactly one line `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>` and a newline to stdout. It prints nothing to stderr and exits with status 0.
For a file containing 'café' encoded as UTF-8, `wordcount PATH` prints `words: 1 characters: 4 bytes: 5 lines: 0`.
For an empty file, `wordcount PATH` prints `words: 0 characters: 0 bytes: 0 lines: 0`.

For each SPEC-0004 byte sample, `wordcount PATH` and `wordcount -` print identical four-field lines. The expected lines are: b'a b
' gives `words: 2 characters: 2 bytes: 4 lines: 1`. b'a
b
' gives `words: 2 characters: 2 bytes: 6 lines: 2`. b'ab' gives `words: 2 characters: 2 bytes: 4 lines: 2`. 'café naïve 日本
' gives `words: 3 characters: 11 bytes: 20 lines: 1`.

hello.cli.main reads the input once as raw bytes. It passes those same bytes to hello.byte_counter.count_bytes after they decode successfully. It never re-encodes decoded text or calls os.stat, os.path.getsize or Path.stat for the count.
Existing tests that assert the three-field success line are updated to the four-field line, and no other assertion in them changes.
README.md documents the `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>` line and the byte rule (raw input bytes before decoding). It states that the three-field form no longer applies.
All four Quality Gate commands exit 0 on the finished change.
regression_guardrails: The word count <N>, character count <M> and line count <L> keep the unchanged SPEC-0001, SPEC-0002 and SPEC-0003 rules.

A file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 still prints exactly one line `wordcount: error: file is not valid UTF-8 text: PATH` to stderr. It prints nothing to stdout, so no byte count appears, and exits with status 1.
`wordcount -` with invalid UTF-8 on stdin still prints `wordcount: error: file is not valid UTF-8 text: <stdin>`, nothing to stdout, and exits 1.
A missing path and an unreadable path keep their existing one-line stderr messages, empty stdout and exit status 1.
No error case writes a Python traceback to stderr.
The invocation is unchanged: one PATH or '-' argument, no new flags. No argument or extra arguments still give argparse usage and exit status 2, and no argument does not read stdin.
A file literally named '-' is still counted through `wordcount ./-`.
hello.counter.count_words, hello.characters.count_characters and hello.lines.count_lines return the same values as before.
The input is still decoded once along the shared file and stdin path, with no newline translation.
pyproject.toml [project].dependencies stays empty, `uv lock --check` exits 0, and the AGENTS.md Toolchain table and Judgment Boundaries stay word for word.
`import hello` still succeeds with every name it exported before, src/hello/py.typed remains, and the src layout is unchanged.

SPEC.context:
Users who size buffers, uploads or storage currently run a second tool to learn the input's byte size. wordcount already reads each input once as raw bytes, along one path shared by files and standard input (SPEC-0004).

This change adds a byte field to the success line, right after characters. The count comes from the raw bytes of that single read, so a file and '-' always agree. Invalid UTF-8 input keeps the existing error, with no byte count.
api_contracts: `wordcount PATH` and `wordcount -` print `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>` on success, exit 0
Error output and exit statuses unchanged (ADR-0004)
data_models: The raw bytes of the single read, passed unchanged to count_bytes
The decoded text, passed to count_words, count_characters and count_lines
dependencies: Shared single read and decode path for file and stdin (SPEC-0004, ADR-0009)
constraints: Standard library only, no runtime dependencies
The input is read once, and the byte count uses those raw bytes
No new command-line flags or arguments
No byte count is printed on any error
Comprehension quizzes are not used for this feature

decisions.text: We will print exactly one labeled line, `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>`, on stdout for every successful wordcount run, and never print a count on error. This supersedes ADR-0008.
decisions.title: Four-field labeled success output for wordcount (supersedes ADR-0008)
decisions.context: ADR-0008 fixes a three-field line. Users want the byte size beside the character count, and approved the order words, characters, bytes, lines.
alternatives: Append bytes after lines: rejected, the user asked for bytes beside characters
Opt-in flag for bytes: rejected, it adds an argument and hides the field by default
Keep ADR-0008 and use a second tool: rejected, it leaves the problem unsolved
positive_consequences: One run gives all four counts
The field order follows the user's request
negative_consequences: Scripts matching the three-field line break after upgrading
Existing tests that assert the three-field line must change

enforcement.rule: A successful wordcount run prints exactly `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>` and a newline

decisions.text: We will count bytes in a pure function hello.byte_counter.count_bytes in src/hello/byte_counter.py. It receives the raw bytes of the single input read, never a re-encoding or a file-system size.
decisions.title: Raw-byte rule in a pure byte counter
decisions.context: Standard input has no file-system size and cannot be read twice. Re-encoding decoded text measures the decoded text, not the input.
alternatives: Take the size from os.stat: rejected, stdin has none, so file and '-' would diverge
Re-encode the decoded text: rejected, it could drift from the raw input
Compute len() inline in hello.cli: rejected, it breaks the pure-counter pattern of ADR-0002, ADR-0005 and ADR-0007
positive_consequences: File and '-' give the same count for the same bytes
The byte rule is testable without I/O
negative_consequences: A one-line function adds a module
hello.cli must keep the raw bytes alongside the decoded text

enforcement.rule: hello.byte_counter performs no file, process or console I/O and imports only the standard library
hello.cli passes the bytes of its single read to count_bytes and never re-encodes text or reads a file-system size for it
enforcement.mechanism: Code review of src/hello/cli.py against this rule

architecture_change.summary: Add a pure byte-counter fed the raw input bytes from the single read, and print a four-field success line, so users get byte size beside characters (STRAT-0005).

added.name: Byte counter
added.owns: The byte rule: the byte count is the number of raw bytes in the input as read, before any decoding. It counts the bytes it is given and returns the number.
added.does_not_own: Reading the input, decoding, or deriving bytes from decoded text. It does not own the word, character or line rules, argument handling, output formatting or exit codes. It never touches the filesystem or the process.

changed.name: hello
changed.owns: Giving users local, dependency-free text utilities. It currently reports the word count, the non-whitespace character count, the raw byte count and the terminated-line count of one input in a single invocation. The input is one text file or standard input.
changed.does_not_own: Other text statistics beyond word, character, byte and line counts, such as longest line or per-line output. Byte counts for input that is not valid UTF-8. Several inputs in one invocation, totals, implicit or auto-detected stdin, non-UTF-8 encodings, or distribution through a public package index.
changed.deployment: Installed from the repository into a local Python environment on the user's machine.
changed.technology: Python (current stable release), standard library only

changed.name: hello command-line package
changed.owns: The installable src-layout hello package and its console command. The command takes one file path, or the '-' argument for standard input. It prints that input's word, character, byte and line counts on one line and exits with a status code.
changed.does_not_own: Any network access, persistent state, configuration files, or third-party runtime dependencies. Command-line flags or arguments beyond the single PATH or '-' argument. Reading standard input when no argument is given.
changed.deployment: Run as a local process on the user's machine after installing the package from the repository into the project environment.
changed.technology: Python standard library; console entry point declared in pyproject.toml; environment managed with the existing lockfile tooling

changed.name: Word-count command
changed.owns: Parsing the single argument: a file path, or '-' for standard input. It reads the chosen source once as raw bytes and decodes them as UTF-8 along one shared path. It passes those same raw bytes to the byte counter. It passes the decoded text to the word, character and line counters. It prints the four counts as one line in the form `words: <N> characters: <M> bytes: <B> lines: <L>`. It turns a missing file, an unreadable file or undecodable content into a one-line stderr message, a non-zero exit status and empty stdout, with no byte count. Messages for standard input name `<stdin>`, and file-path messages and statuses are unchanged.
changed.does_not_own: The definition of what a word, a visible character, a byte count or a line is, or counting logic of any kind. It does not read the input a second time, take the size from the file system, or re-encode decoded text. It does not decode text a second time, along a separate path per source, or with newline translation. It does not read standard input when no argument is given. A file literally named '-' is reached only through './-'.

relations_added.description: Passes the raw bytes from the single read of the file or standard input, after they decode successfully, in an in-process function call. It receives the integer byte count.
